_comment: Neo-Industrial (Entry 10, Cluster C) — Production Brand Config. Promoted from v0.9.1 test fixture for B4-S4 Breadth Stress Test. Stages 1–3 complete (Boards A/B/C + Stage 2 validation PASS 0C/0H). Stage 3 resolutions: display font IBM Plex Sans Condensed (open-source; Druk Wide for client deployment), loading resolved to Google Fonts, alarm-high-priority normalized to kebab-case, light scheme omitted (dark-native, Stage 5 dark-only, light requires separate designer confirmation). 0 PROVISIONAL fields remaining. FIDELITY_WARN expected (Mode D inferred values, no designer review — correct for stress test). Restore HeyHi config after Stage 6: python3 scripts/switch-brand.py --config heyhi

brand.name: Neo-Industrial
brand.description: Dark-native industrial interface system built on ISA-101 High Performance HMI conventions. Monospace as primary body voice. Near-neutral dark foundation communicates operational authority through visible structure and precision typography. Color is functional, never decorative — chromatic signals indicate state, not brand personality.
brand.personality: Austere, declarative, and precise. The interface communicates that it builds things. Heavy condensed grotesque headers give way to a monospace-dominant body register. Hard-bordered zones, dense information count, and a five-state ISA-101 functional color system produce operational interfaces for manufacturing, industrial IoT, and construction tech.
brand.style_notes: Cluster C — Neo-Industrial (Entry 10). Dark-native config: meta.default_scheme is 'dark'. Token flat structure reflects the active dark scheme. Both schemes held in tokens.color.schemes per ADR-006 Option C. WS3 PARTIAL — intentional: display zone governed by Augmented Fourth 1.414x; body/data zone fixed at 14-16px monospace outside the scale system. Zone separation is architectural, not a calibration error. Document zone rules in every client implementation brief for Neo-Industrial engagements. WS8 PASS — Augmented Fourth (1.414x) exceeds the Major Third (1.25x) WS8 threshold; no incoherence risk. WS6 PASS — documented ISA-101 exception: ISA-101 requires high-contrast chromatic signals against an achromatic dark foundation. The ±15% saturation rule does not apply when functional color serves safety-critical state communication. Semantic saturation departure from the near-zero primary accent is required, not a mistake. ISA-101 further requires that color is never the sole indicator: shape, symbol, or label must accompany every status signal (approximately 8% of male operators have color vision deficiency). Stage 3 resolution: display font is IBM Plex Sans Condensed for this stress test (open-source). Client deployment should use Druk Wide with Commercial Type license.
brand.agent_context_snippet: Neo-Industrial produces interfaces that communicate operational authority through visible structure and monospace precision. Heavy display type at section headers gives way to a monospace-dominant body register — this is not just a data accent, it is the primary voice throughout body and data zones (JetBrains Mono, 14–16px fixed, outside the Augmented Fourth scale system). Color is ISA-101 functional only: gray = nominal, green = running, yellow = abnormal, orange = high-priority alarm, red = critical, blue = manual mode — every chromatic signal requires secondary shape or symbol encoding; avoid soft surfaces, warm tones, rounded corners (zero border radius throughout), gradient fills, or any decorative color use.

display.use: Section headers and operational labels only. Heavy weight at display zone scale (h1–h4). All-caps for system status labels. Governs display zone exclusively — body/data zone uses monospace. NOTE: This stress test uses IBM Plex Sans Condensed (open-source). Client deployments should use Druk Wide (Commercial Type license required) for the full Neo-Industrial intent.

body.use: Primary body and data register throughout. All measured values, status readouts, data tables, operational prose, and UI labels. Monospace alignment ensures fixed-width value columns. 14–16px fixed range — not governed by the Augmented Fourth scale.

utility.use: Navigation labels, form fields, timestamps, metadata. Same monospace family as body to maintain the fixed-width grid throughout.

prohibited.value: Any warm hue (yellow-red undertone > 10° hue angle)
prohibited.reason: Warm tones contradict the cool precision register and weaken functional color authority

prohibited.value: Gradient fills on backgrounds or panels
prohibited.reason: Gradients add surface warmth and softness — both are anti-mood for Neo-Industrial

prohibited.value: Decorative color use for brand personality
prohibited.reason: In ISA-101 systems, every chromatic appearance signals a state change. Decorative color creates false state alarms.

contrast_notes: Primary text (#E8E8E8) on primary background (#141414): ~18:1 — exceeds WCAG AAA (7:1)
Secondary text (#A0A0A0) on primary background (#141414): ~6.3:1 — exceeds WCAG AA (4.5:1)
Label text (#B0B0B0) on primary background (#141414): ~7.5:1 — exceeds WCAG AA
Tertiary text (#707070) on primary background (#141414): ~3.8:1 — AA large text only; restrict to non-functional annotation
Disabled text (#4A4A4A) on primary background (#141414): ~2.3:1 — intentionally below AA; decorative only
Warning (#D4A500) on dark background (#141414): ~8.05:1 — exceeds WCAG AA for indicator-scale use
Alarm high-priority (#E67E22) on dark background (#141414): ~6.47:1 — exceeds WCAG AA; always paired with shape encoding per ISA-101
Success green (#2D8659) on dark background (#141414): ~4.09:1 — meets AA large text; acceptable at indicator scale per ISA-101 usage pattern
Info blue (#2980B9) on dark background (#141414): ~4.28:1 — meets AA large text; acceptable at indicator scale
Critical red (#C0392B) on dark background (#141414): ~3.39:1 — meets AA large text threshold for indicator-scale use; always requires secondary shape encoding
Focus ring blue (#3498DB) on primary background (#141414): ~4.5:1 — meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13 (3:1 minimum)

spacing.rhythm: 4px modular scale. Dense information count throughout — no breathing-room padding. Zone boundaries established by 1px borders, not whitespace intervals.

motion.principles: State changes only — thresholds trigger, values update, indicators flip. No entrance animations, no choreography, no decorative motion. If something moves, a state changed. Exception: alarm-high-priority may flash at 200ms interval as secondary indicator (shape/symbol encoding required alongside flash).

voice.tone: Declarative and precise. Label the state. Name the value. Instructions are operational, not conversational. The interface does not explain itself — it reports.
prohibited_patterns: Questions as UI copy ('Want to try...?')
voice.cta_style: Direct and operational. Verb + target. 'Start monitoring.' 'Acknowledge alarm.' 'Override value.' Never soft.

formatting.units: Adjacent to value, never separated (e.g., '14.7 psi', not '14.7   psi')

empty_states.pattern: State the inactive condition directly, then provide the operational action. 'NO ACTIVE ALARMS. MONITOR.' Never 'Nothing here yet.'

error_messages.pattern: FAULT: [system component]. [Action verb] [target] to [outcome]. Never apologetic. Always actionable.
error_messages.tone: Declarative. No hedging. Operator needs to act, not sympathize.

tooltips.pattern: Value definition or unit clarification only — one line, no narrative. 'PSI: pounds per square inch — gauge pressure.' Not 'This shows you the current pressure.'
tooltips.tone: Technical label. No articles where possible.

buttons_ctas.pattern: Verb + target. Imperative. No softening articles or future tense. 'Acknowledge Alarm.' 'Override Value.' 'Start Monitoring.' Never 'Click here to acknowledge.'
buttons_ctas.verb_preference: Operational verbs: Acknowledge, Override, Start, Stop, Reset, Confirm, Cancel
buttons_ctas.style: ALL-CAPS for critical actions (ACKNOWLEDGE, OVERRIDE). Title Case for standard operations.

form_labels.pattern: Field name only. No helper text unless a unit or format is required. 'Flow Rate (psi)' not 'Enter the current flow rate in pounds per square inch.'
form_labels.case: Title Case for labels. ALL-CAPS for critical or safety-related fields.
form_labels.placeholder_policy: Placeholder shows format only, never instructions. '14.7' not 'Enter value here'

notifications.pattern: State label first, then source system, then action if required. 'ALARM HIGH — Flow Zone 4. Acknowledge or escalate.'

loading_states.pattern: INITIALIZING followed by the system or data source name. 'INITIALIZING SENSOR FEED.' Not 'Loading...' or a spinner with no label.

onboarding.pattern: Not applicable — Neo-Industrial targets operational interfaces (SCADA, monitoring dashboards, industrial control panels). Onboarding copy patterns do not apply to this context.

meta.version_history: v0.9.0 — Mode D re-run with ADR-006 tokens.color.schemes block applied (Session 9, 2026-03-24). Previous version was blocked at v0.5 pending dark mode architecture decision. v0.9.1 — quality audit applied: _note fields removed from token namespaces, consolidated into meta.implementation_notes; WS6 corrected to PASS; provisional_fields index completed; brand.style_notes corrected (WS8 removed from PARTIAL list). v1.0.0-stress-test — Promoted for B4-S4 Breadth Stress Test (2026-04-08): display font updated to IBM Plex Sans Condensed (open-source stress-test variant; Druk Wide for client deployment), loading resolved to Google Fonts, alarm_high_priority normalized to alarm-high-priority (kebab-case), gate_status and layout blocks added, brand.cluster + brand.style_entry + brand.agent_context_snippet added, light scheme confirmed out-of-scope for Stage 5. Promote to v1.0.0-confirmed after designer confirmation round.
meta.color_strategy: Achromatic dark foundation (near-neutral deep charcoals) with ISA-101 five-state functional color system. Gray is nominal — system at rest. Chromatic signals (green, yellow, orange, red, blue) indicate operational states. Color never decorative. Every chromatic appearance communicates a state change.
meta.grid_structure: 12-column explicit grid. Column lines visible or strongly implied by 1px borders. Wide content width (1440px max). Dense information count — rows, columns, and measurement displays share vertical space. Each zone is discrete and bounded by a hard 1px border.
meta.spacing_reasoning: 4px base unit, dense tier system. No breathing-room padding — industrial interfaces prioritize information density over comfort. Zone separation via 1px structural borders, not whitespace. Section-level values (24px, 48px) are functional separators, not decorative.
meta.scale_reasoning: Augmented Fourth 1.414x governs the display zone (h1–h4) only. Creates the high-contrast scale jump between heavy display headers and dense monospace body — drama communicates authority before utility. Body/data zone is intentionally outside the scale system: fixed at 14–16px monospace to preserve fixed-width column alignment in data tables and measurement displays. This is the zone-separation architecture that makes WS3 PARTIAL intentional rather than a calibration error. WS8 PASS: Augmented Fourth exceeds the Major Third (1.25x) WS8 threshold — no heading-hierarchy ambiguity risk.

implementation_notes.display_font_stress_test: This config uses IBM Plex Sans Condensed for the stress test (open-source, Google Fonts). The Neo-Industrial style entry specifies Druk Wide (Commercial Type) as the production display font. Client deployments must acquire a Druk Wide license and update tokens.typography.families.display.family and tokens.typography.loading accordingly. IBM Plex Sans Condensed at weight 700/900 provides a close structural proxy for stress-test validation purposes.
implementation_notes.body_register: ADR-004 optional field. type_personality: grotesque captures the display voice only. body_register: monospace-primary encodes the D4+D10 hybrid — heavy grotesque at display scale over monospace as primary body/data voice. Mode D implementations must not apply a single grotesque family throughout.
implementation_notes.zone_separation: Display zone (h1–h4) governed by Augmented Fourth 1.414x from 16px base. Body/data zone (body, label, caption, data) fixed at 14–16px monospace — outside the scale system. This is the zone-separation architecture that makes WS3 PARTIAL intentional. WS8 PASS: Augmented Fourth (1.414x) exceeds the Major Third (1.25x) WS8 threshold — no heading-hierarchy ambiguity risk.
implementation_notes.scheme_strategy: Dark-native config. Flat tokens.color.* reflect the active dark scheme. Full parallel schemes in tokens.color.schemes per ADR-006 Option C. Light scheme is PROVISIONAL — dark-native entries require designer confirmation for any light mode implementation. Light scheme is explicitly out-of-scope for Stage 5 Mode D build.
implementation_notes.light_scheme_stage5_scope: Stage 5 Mode D build targets the dark scheme exclusively. Light scheme PROVISIONAL values must not be used in any Stage 5 component. If light mode support is required for a client deployment, restart from this config and initiate a separate light scheme confirmation round with the designer.
implementation_notes.accent_isa101: Gray is the nominal state in ISA-101 — a system at rest, a pump stopped, a value within range. No decorative chromatic accent. Primary accent is cool mid-gray (#A0A0A0). Color enters only when a system state requires attention (see semantic tokens).
implementation_notes.alarm_high_priority: ADR-007 Extension 3 — ISA-101 High Performance HMI orange alarm. High-priority alarm state between abnormal-deviation yellow (#D4A500) and critical-hazard red (#C0392B). Requires immediate operator response. alarm-high-priority must ALWAYS have a secondary shape/symbol encoding — color cannot be the sole indicator per ISA-101 (~8% male operators with color vision deficiency). NOTE: Naming normalized to kebab-case at v1 promotion (was alarm_high_priority in v0.9.x — known snake_case defect, now fixed).
implementation_notes.nominal_state: Gray = nominal operational state. Equipment at rest, value within range, process normal. No chromatic signal in nominal state.
implementation_notes.schemes: ADR-006 Option C — Scheme namespacing for dark-native configs. Dark is the active default scheme. Light is a provisional alternative. Migration path to W3C DTCG $modes documented in ADR-006.
implementation_notes.touch_target: ADR-007 Extension 2. Industrial interfaces include field worker tablet and panel contexts. 40px floor for industrial IoT; 44px comfortable for operator panels where gloved or obstructed touch is possible.
implementation_notes.elevation_strategy: Flat — surfaces are coplanar. No shadow depth. Zone separation achieved entirely through 1px borders and background tonal shifts, not elevation.
implementation_notes.radius_strategy: Zero border radius throughout. Hard-edged surfaces communicate precision and structural integrity. Any rounding contradicts the Neo-Industrial register.
implementation_notes.focus_ring: ADR-007 Extension 1. Focus ring uses ISA-101 manual-mode blue (#3498DB) against dark backgrounds — achieves ~4.5:1 contrast against primary background (#141414), exceeding WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13 minimum (3:1). Consistent with the 'blue = manual mode / operator override' semantic assignment.
implementation_notes.naming_convention: All multi-word semantic tokens use kebab-case (success-bg, warning-bg, alarm-high-priority, alarm-high-priority-bg). Previous snake_case usage (alarm_high_priority) was a known defect in v0.9.x, normalized at v1 promotion. Treat kebab-case as the convention for all future Neo-Industrial token additions.
implementation_notes.completeness_score_note: completeness_score: 82 (estimated). All five token families specified; layout block present; voice complete. Gaps: field_provenance not populated, light scheme PROVISIONAL. Run validate.py for authoritative score.
implementation_notes.fidelity_score_note: fidelity_score: 65 (estimated). Most values are 'inferred' from Mode D moodboard extraction rather than 'extracted' from a confirmed Figma source. Designer confirmation round would elevate this to the 80+ range required for version promotion to v1.0.0-confirmed.

Light scheme requires a separate designer confirmation round before population. See meta.implementation_notes.light_scheme_stage5_scope.
